This page is a map of [the documentation][idx]. It does not repeat the content. It shows **what is where**, **how the pages relate to each other**, and **in which order to read them** depending on what you want to do.

It covers the ten content pages of the site menu. *About* and *Privacy Policy* are not covered.

::: {.callout-tip}
## The one-paragraph version
The documentation helps you to choose **the simplest setup that meets your current needs** (a hosted service first, then local install, virtual machine, Docker Compose, Kubernetes) and to understand it well enough to find your way in each tool's own documentation. Linux, containers, storage, backups, security, data protection, assemblies of several tools, semantic graphs and LLMs are covered in separate pages that point to each other.
:::

# The complexity ladder

The core idea of the guide is to choose the simplest setup that meets your current needs, and to check first whether a hosted service already exists. When a ready-made image is available, Docker and then Docker Compose are the easiest ways to set a platform up, and Kubernetes is the step up when you need scale and availability. Installing by hand, in a virtual machine or on bare metal, is the fallback when no usable image exists or the application cannot be containerised: it is more work to install, update and maintain. The boxes carry the section of the step-by-step guide where each option is explained.


[Linux basics](index.qmd#sec-linux), [scalability](index.qmd#sec-scalability), [databases](index.qmd#sec-databases), [security](index.qmd#sec-security), [the *Backups and Security* page][bak], [automation](index.qmd#sec-automatize-the-setup), and [the choice of tools](index.qmd#sec-many-choices) are not tied to one rung. | Block | What you get | Learning difficulty stated in the guide |
|---|---|---|
| A · Orientation | Scope, the five levels of setup, six common rules (keep difficulty under control, level of service, plan for problems not features, document changes, use version control) | none |
| B · Foundations | Commands, folders, users and groups, cgroups, firewall/SSH/VPN, remote display, web servers; vocabulary for bare metal, emulation and virtualisation | easy to very hard, "intermediate" for a cloud installation |
| C · Containers | Image, container, volume, Compose; a typical compose file with `.env`, health checks and YAML anchors; namespaces, bind mounts; multi-stage Dockerfiles | Docker easy, Compose easy/medium, Dockerfile medium |
| D · Orchestration | Pods, nodes, replicas, declarative manifests; when Kubernetes is overkill | medium/hard |
| E · Other solutions | Proxmox, OpenStack (Nova, Neutron, Cinder, Swift, Ceph, Magnum…), Nomad, Swarm, ECS, GKE, Cloud Run, six Apache projects | not stated |
| F · Cross-cutting | Vertical vs. horizontal scaling, relational vs. other databases, security checklist | not stated |
| G · Operations | Assemblies, Puppet/Ansible/Terraform, CI/CD and GitOps, choosing tools | not stated |

# The decision tree, condensed

The page [Technical platform decision tree][dt] contains the full tree. This is a shortened version to see the logic at a glance. The full tree adds a branch for institution-managed virtual servers (check backups, snapshots and load balancing there).

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-decision
%%| fig-cap: "Condensed decision tree (see the decision tree page for the full version)"
flowchart TD
  classDef q fill:#fef3c7,stroke:#d97706,color:#111
  classDef r fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#16a34a,color:#111

  S(["Start<br/>(repeat for each platform of an assembly)"])
  Q1{"Hosted service from<br/>institution or consortium?"}:::q
  Q2{"24/7 availability<br/>needed?"}:::q
  Q3{"Managed Kubernetes<br/>available?"}:::q
  Q4{"Skills, platform fits Kubernetes,<br/>benefits outweigh complexity?"}:::q
  Q5{"Familiar with Docker / Compose<br/>and platform supports it?"}:::q
  Q6{"Specific need for<br/>orchestration (HA, load balancing)?"}:::q
  Q7{"Can you create and<br/>manage VMs?"}:::q
  Q8{"Can you install on a<br/>dedicated physical server?"}:::q

  R1["Use the service<br/>(check API access)"]:::r
  R2["Kubernetes-based stack"]:::r
  R3["Swarm, Nomad or similar"]:::r
  R4["Docker Compose"]:::r
  R5["Single VM<br/>(image or manual install)"]:::r
  R6["Bare metal<br/>(ready-made image if possible)"]:::r
  R7["External service"]:::r

  S --> Q1
  Q1 -->|yes| R1
  Q1 -->|no| Q2
  Q2 -->|yes| Q3
  Q2 -->|no| Q5
  Q3 -->|"yes, supported"| R2
  Q3 -->|no| Q4
  Q4 -->|yes| R2
  Q4 -->|no| Q5
  Q5 -->|yes| Q6
  Q5 -->|no| Q7
  Q6 -->|yes| R3
  Q6 -->|no| R4
  Q7 -->|yes| R5
  Q7 -->|no| Q8
  Q8 -->|yes| R6
  Q8 -->|no| R7
```

::: {.callout-note}
The tree deliberately leaves out OpenStack and Proxmox (OpenStack is very complex; Proxmox only makes sense if your IT does not offer enough servers *and* someone has the time to run it). It also comes *after* a data management plan (see RDMKit).
:::

## Kubernetes

# Suggested reading paths

| Path | You are… | Read in this order |
|---|---|---|
| **1 · First contact** (about 1–2 h) | new to the topic | [Onboarding][onb] → [Decision tree][dt] → [When to use each setup][when-to] and [Common remarks][common-remarks] → [Docker][containers] and [Docker Compose][compose] → [Backups][backups] |
| **2 · Deploying with Compose** | installing a platform on one server | [Linux][linux] as needed → [Docker][containers] through [Dockerfile][dockerfile] → [Volumes and databases][data-volumes-db] → [Backups and Security][bak] → [Automation][automation] |
| **3 · Towards Kubernetes** | already comfortable with Compose | [Compose to Kubernetes][compose-k8s] → [Kubernetes showcase][k8s-part-1] → [Kubernetes overview][k8s-part-2] → [Kubernetes storage][k8s-storage] → [alternative solutions][other-solutions] |
| **4 · Data protection** | responsible for sensitive data | [Personal data][personal-data] → [Pseudonymization][pse] → [Assembly graph safety][asm-graphs] → [LLM data handling][llm-data] |
| **5 · Interoperability and FAIR** | connecting and describing data | [Semantic graph scope][sem-scope] and [RDM uses][sem-rdm] → [Assembly graphs][asm-graphs] → [Semantic graph how-to][sem-how] → [LLMs in RDM][llm] |
| **6 · Working with AI tools** | using LLMs in research data work | [LLMs in RDM][llm] → [LLM and knowledge graphs][sem-llm] and [SPARQL with LLM][sem-sparql] → [LLM use in assemblies][asm-llm] |

# Outside the site

The documentation points to a few external resources repeatedly:

- **RDMKit** (<https://rdmkit.elixir-europe.org/>): the wider context of research data management. The guide recommends starting there and using these pages for the technical depth.
- **FAIR-DMP-Registry** (<https://dekcd.github.io/FAIR-DMP-Registry/>): the list of data management platforms the guide has in mind.
- **Hosted services** named in the guide: De.NBI Cloud, European Open Science Cloud, EGI Federation, GWDG Academic Cloud and others.
